description: Attribute-based narrowing for knowledge resources. ABAC decides whether a caller that already holds a signed identity may read a resource; it never grants a capability, never widens a scope and never becomes a knowledge channel. Subject attributes come from a verified registry entry or a signed session grant. Resource attributes come from the ingestion classification record, not from the caller. Unknown or missing attributes are denied.

ingestion.rule: The ingestion writer records classification in frontmatter; readers use that field and never accept a caller-supplied label. A page without the field is legacy and uses the path fallback. An unknown or malformed field is denied, never guessed.

node.source: a registry entry verified by shared/sparknet-authz.py plus the local role vault id
node.vault_id_source: local role configuration; registry-schema.json deliberately excludes a vault path from the signed identity

user.source: a signed grant verified by the guard plus the local vault id
user.vault_scope_empty: valid; node-level configuration only, so every knowledge read is denied by the scope check

rules: A subject is accepted only after signature verification by the one authz implementation. This module consumes the verified result and never verifies a signature itself.
A missing or unknown classification is denied; there is no default.
A missing provenance digest is denied; a page without provenance is a guess.
The authority class is never readable through ABAC, by any subject.
A user subject reads only its own vault and only within the signed scope.
A node subject reads the shared or fabric corpus only with the mapped capability.
Shared and fabric resources must be public or internal; confidential and restricted pages never enter a shared corpus.
Personal prefixes and names are never shared, even if a caller labels them public.
A department boundary exists only when both sides carry an attested department; crossing it requires cross-department-share.
A requested scope must be a subset of the effective scope; a request can narrow, never widen.
A decision record is evidence, not authority. It carries no capability and no signature.
